title: Mocking Concrete Structs via Empty Interfaces
pattern: Creating an abstract interface (trait) with only a single implementation, solely to enable mocking of a stable, deterministic, local concrete type in tests.
why_bad: It creates high interface ceremony and file pollution. If a concrete type contains only pure mathematical, logical, or state-based code with no volatile external side-effects, it can be tested and used directly without any mocking infrastructure.
detection: A public trait with exactly one implementation in the codebase, where the implementation logic does not interact with any network, filesystem, or database boundaries.
counterexample: Interfaces designed to abstract truly volatile external services (like third-party payment gateways or cloud-based notification systems).
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright, *Software Engineering at Google* (2020), Chapter 13 ("Mocking"), pp. 245-248.
